source.title: The Deep Bootstrap: Good Online Learners are Good Offline Generalizers
source.authors: Preetum Nakkiran; Behnam Neyshabur; Hanie Sedghi

record.file_problem: The complete paper text is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Compares convolutional and fully connected networks on CIFAR-5m using test performance, bearing on the architecture comparison in V3; it does not reproduce the original studies’ specific setups.
record.gate_note: The random-label discussion in Section 5 states what the framework would predict, but reports no new random-label experiment. Width-varying ResNet results and other figures concern settings outside the specific conditions of the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study tests V3 in a new image distribution: convolutional and fully connected networks trained from scratch with SGD on CIFAR-5m. Its own results explicitly show better held-out performance for convolutional networks.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the D-CONV/D-FC result. More broadly, the authors propose that offline generalization can often be understood through online population optimization because Real and Ideal World test soft-errors remain close until finite-data training converges. They explicitly acknowledge larger bootstrap errors with limited data, without augmentation, and in some other settings.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a CIFAR-5m task and the D-CONV/D-FC architectures; measures test error through the paper’s Real/Ideal World framework rather than reproducing the cited study’s setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that bootstrap error can be larger at limited sample sizes and without data augmentation; data augmentation typically reduces it. These are framework-level findings, not separate V3 architecture-comparison results.

fits_no_version.finding: Real and Ideal World test soft-errors are often close, and faster online population optimization accompanies better offline generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested image classifiers, fresh-sample and repeated-sample training often produce similar held-out soft-error until finite-data training converges.

record.problems: The architecture comparison’s plotted results have no numeric values in the supplied text. CIFAR-5m is synthetic and labeled by a model; the paper says it is not identical to CIFAR-10. The tested D-CONV/D-FC comparison does not cover the full range of conditions in V3.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. Figures 2–4 vary architectures, learning rates, sample sizes, or ResNet widths for Real-versus-Ideal comparisons, but do not test the specific claim versions’ conditions and measures.

untested.parts: No new experiment jointly establishes random-label fitting capacity, chance-level random-label test accuracy, and natural-label generalization.
No reported result establishes continued improvement beyond the width required for interpolation in converged one-hidden-layer ReLU networks. The ResNet width plots do not establish this comparison.

The contribution of local connectivity separately from weight sharing; learned sparse local connections; convolutional initialization of fully connected networks; and replication on the original datasets.
No explicit adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance comparison under a defined tuning budget. Adam experiments primarily compare Real and Ideal Worlds.
No batch-size intervention comparing held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets or adapted recipes.
No dropout intervention. Including dropout in the architectures does not test its effect.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or ranking of generalization-gap predictors.
No removal of memorized examples and matched random-removal control.

missing.what: The independent ResNet-18 versus MLP architecture comparison: the Introduction explicitly reports better finite-data generalization for the convnet. Record held-out soft-error trajectories or the qualitative comparison, including the matched SGD recipe and stopping rule.
missing.locator: Introduction, Figure 1; Appendix B.1, Figure 8; Appendix D.1

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V3. CIFAR-5m contains generated images with model-assigned labels, so the support concerns that distribution. The supplied text provides qualitative architecture comparisons but no readable numerical figure values. Missing tests of V3's mechanisms warrant untested entries, not limits_scope verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment fitting random labels or comparing held-out performance on random and natural labels.
No one-hidden-layer ReLU width sweep around the interpolation threshold.
Does not test MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 or SVHN, learned sparse local connections, or convolutional initialization of a fully connected network.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers and SGD on held-out performance under the version’s tuning conditions.
No large-batch versus small-batch comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No dropout intervention or comparison with dropout and weight decay removed.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized examples or comparison with random-example removal.
